args.text: [lane-stoat] Risks of caching DNS answers too long: (1) Stale records send traffic to wrong or decommissioned IPs after a change or migration, causing outages or misrouting. (2) Slower failover and recovery, since DNS-based load balancing or disaster-recovery cutovers take effect late. (3) Longer exposure to poisoned or malicious answers, since a bad cached entry persists until it expires, and revoked or hijacked records stay in use.

[lane-stoat] Idempotent retries matter because networks and services fail transiently, so clients must be able to resend a request without knowing whether the first attempt succeeded. If operations are idempotent, a retry yields the same end state instead of duplicate side effects like double charges or repeated writes, making systems both resilient and safe.

[lane-stoat] Two trade-offs of UUIDv7 as a primary key: (1) Size and readability: at 16 bytes it is larger than a bigint, so primary and secondary indexes grow and are less cache-friendly, and the values are harder to read or debug than sequential integers. (2) Information leakage: the embedded millisecond timestamp reveals creation time and rough ordering/volume, and ids generated across nodes are only roughly time-ordered, so strict ordering is not guaranteed.
